content.text: Section 23 is a bare heading with no substantive text, and there are no other verification, inspection, or monitoring rights binding us anywhere in the agreement. Section 22 is the only audit clause.

input.quote: 22.1 Vendor may audit Customer's compliance with licence quantities no more than once in any twelve-month period, on at least thirty days' prior written notice, during normal business hours, and in a manner that does not unreasonably disrupt Customer. An audit will be conducted off-site where practicable by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality.
input.rationale: Section 22 is the only provision granting audit/verification rights against us; Section 23 ("Records and Customer Assurance") is a bare heading with no substantive text, and a document-wide search found no other inspection, monitoring, metering or telemetry-based verification right binding Customer. Section 22 meets the preferred position on every material term: frequency limited to once in any twelve-month period, at least thirty days' prior written notice, normal business hours, off-site where practicable, an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, Vendor bearing audit costs unless underpayment exceeds five percent (better than the fallback's 10% threshold), and an express bar on Vendor or its auditor accessing Customer systems directly, unrelated Customer Data, privileged material, or another supplier's confidential information — so the walk-away risks (unlimited/unannounced audits or remote system access) are excluded. Section 22.3 adds further customer-favourable protections (findings are our Confidential Information, use restricted to enforcement, copy of the final report, and payment of a shortfall resolving the audited quantity issue). No redline needed.
